questions.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?

options.text: Each of the players are given a trophy.
Every boy and girl have their task.
Either of the answers is acceptable.
Neither she nor her friends is ready.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Either of the answers is acceptable .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Option 3, **"Either of the answers is acceptable,"** is grammatically correct because the subject **"either"** is singular and requires a singular verb **"is."**
 
• Option 1, **"Each of the players are given a trophy,"** is incorrect because **"each"** is singular and should be followed by a singular verb **"is."**
 
• Option 2, **"Every boy and girl have their task,"** is incorrect because **"every"** is singular and should be followed by a singular verb **"has."**
 
• Option 4, **"Neither she nor her friends is ready,"** is incorrect because when using **"neither...nor"**, the verb agrees with the subject closer to it. In this case, **"friends"** is plural, so the correct verb would be **"are."**

Correct sentence: *Either of the answers **is acceptable**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agreement with Indefinite Pronouns:**

 
 
• Singular indefinite pronouns (e.g., **"each," "every," "either," "neither"**) take singular verbs.
 
• Example: Each of the students **has** completed their assignment.
 
 
 
• **Neither...Nor and Either...Or:**
 
 
• The verb agrees with the subject closest to it.
 
• Example: Neither the teacher nor the students **are** ready.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Identify Spot the error in the given sentence.

"The principal, along with the teachers, have approved the new syllabus."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. have approved should be replaced with **"has approved"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"The principal"**, which is singular.
 
• The phrase **"along with the teachers"** is additional information and does not affect the verb agreement.
 
• In subject-verb agreement, the verb should agree with the main subject of the sentence.
 
• The correct verb form for a singular subject like **"The principal"** is **"has"**, not **"have"**.

Correct sentence: *The principal, along with the teachers, **has approved** the new syllabus.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rules for Subject-Verb Agreement:**
 
 
• When the subject is singular, the verb must also be singular.
 
• When the subject is plural, the verb must also be plural.
 
• Parenthetical phrases like **"along with," "as well as," "in addition to"**, etc., do not affect the verb agreement.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• The teacher, along with the students, **is** preparing for the event.
 
• The manager, as well as the staff, **has** agreed to the new policy.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate conjunction:**

He was determined to win, ______ the odds were clearly stacked against him.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. although .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence conveys a contrast between two ideas: his determination to win and the fact that the odds were against him.
 
• The conjunction **"although"** is used to show a contrast or contradiction between two clauses in a sentence.
 
• The other options do not fit the context:
 
 
• **Because:** Indicates cause and effect, which is not relevant here.
 
• **Whether:** Indicates uncertainty, which is not appropriate in this sentence.
 
• **Since:** Indicates cause or time, which does not create the contrast required in this context.
 
 

Correct sentence: *He was determined to win, **although** the odds were clearly stacked against him.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Although:**
 
 
• Used to introduce a subordinate clause expressing a contrast.
 
• **Example:** Although he was tired, he continued working.
 
• **Usage:** Often used to connect two ideas that are contradictory or in opposition.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: **HISTORIOGRAPHICAL**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Historical writing .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"historiographical"** is derived from the term **historiography**, which refers to the writing of history and the study of historical methods.
 
• The most appropriate synonym for **"historiographical"** is **"historical writing"**, as it directly relates to the process and methods of recording and analyzing history.
 
• Other options like **Fictional**, **Prophetic**, and **Verbal** are unrelated to the concept of historiography and do not fit the meaning of the word.

Correct sentence: *The term **historiographical** refers to the study and methods of **historical writing**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historiography:** 
 
 
• **Definition:** The writing of history based on the critical examination of sources, the selection of details from authentic materials, and the synthesis of these details into a narrative.
 
• **Example:** The historiographical analysis of World War II looks at how historians have interpreted the causes and outcomes of the war.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Fictional:** Related to stories or narratives created from imagination, not real or historical.
 
• **Prophetic:** Relating to predictions of future events, often based on divine inspiration.
 
• **Verbal:** Relating to spoken or written words, not specific to historical context.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What should come in the place of blank number** ****1?**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Overwhelming**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage describes the air as "**thick**" with the smell of paper and dust. When a sensation is described as thick or dense, it often suggests it is **overwhelming** (अभिभूत कर देने वाला).
 
• The phrase "at once soothing and **overwhelming**" establishes a sensory paradox. It means the scent is comforting (soothing) but also so intense and powerful (overwhelming) that it completely occupies the narrator's senses.
 
• While "Invigorating" (Option 3) means energizing, it doesn't align as well with the description of a "thick" and "earthy" atmosphere as the concept of intensity does.
 
• "**Refreshing**" (Option 1) usually describes light, clean scents, which contrasts with the "dusty" and "earthy" description.
 
• "**Disconcerting**" (Option 4) implies a negative or upsetting feeling, which contradicts the bookstore being called a "refuge."

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

Complete Passage Segment: *The used bookstore was not merely a location where one might purchase books; it was a refuge. The air was thick with the earthy, rich smell of paper and dust, an odd fragrance which was at once soothing and (1) **overwhelming__**. I would spend hours there, running my fingers over the spines of ancient, forgotten books that stood on the shelves. Each novel was another world to discover, and I finally removed a leather-bound book with an odd, yellowed title. Its pages were dry and (2)__________. to the touch, as if one careless turn would make them disintegrate. As I picked up to read the opening lines, the words didn't merely speak a tale-they whisked me off to a whole different world, a place of magical creatures, gallant heroes, and secret spells. The vocabulary was old-fashioned, but impossibly (3)_________, describing gaudy pictures in my head that were more real than the creaky aisles surrounding me. I was amazed by the imagination of the writer, a well that was presumably truly (4)_________. I felt a rush of awe, an appreciation that these tales, as ancient as they were, remained supremely (5) _________ and capable of igniting the imagination of a new generation.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Fragrance (सुगंध):** A pleasant, sweet smell. The author uses this word to show that the narrator finds beauty even in the old, dusty air of the shop.
 
• **Tone and Context:** In competitive exam "Cloze Tests," the adjectives often work in pairs. "Soothing" and "Overwhelming" describe the duality of a deep, nostalgic experience.
 
• **Refuge:** A condition of being safe or sheltered from pursuit, danger, or trouble.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: **Immutable**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Alterable .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **Immutable** means "unchanging over time or unable to be changed."
 
• To find the antonym (opposite meaning), we need a word that implies "capable of being changed."
 
• Among the options:
 
 
• **Unchanging**: Synonym of "immutable," not the correct answer.
 
• **Fixed**: Similar in meaning to "immutable," not the correct answer.
 
• **Alterable**: Means "capable of being altered or changed," which is the opposite of "immutable." This is the correct answer.
 
• **Permanent**: Synonym of "unchanging," not the correct answer.
 
 

Correct sentence: *The most appropriate antonym of "immutable" is **Alterable**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Synonyms:** Words with similar meanings.
 
 
• Example: Immutable - Unchanging, Fixed, Permanent.
 
 
 
• **Antonyms:** Words with opposite meanings.
 
 
• Example: Immutable - Alterable, Changeable, Flexible.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
**Choose the correct one-word substitute for: 

A person who studies the science of the human mind**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. Psychologist .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **psychologist** is a professional who studies the science of the human mind and behavior.
 
• The question asks for a one-word substitute for someone who focuses on the study of the mind and its processes, such as emotions, thoughts, and mental states.
 
• The other options are incorrect as they do not align with the definition provided:
 
 
• **Neurologist:** A medical doctor specializing in the nervous system, not the human mind.
 
• **Psychiatrist:** A medical doctor who diagnoses and treats mental disorders, often with medication.
 
• **Psychopath:** Refers to an individual with a specific personality disorder, not a scientist or professional studying the mind.
 
 

Correct sentence: *A person who studies the science of the human mind is called a **Psychologist**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Psychology:** The scientific study of the mind and behavior. It encompasses various fields such as cognitive, developmental, and social psychology.
 
• **Psychologist vs Psychiatrist:** While both deal with mental health, psychologists primarily use therapy and research, whereas psychiatrists are medical doctors who can prescribe medication.
 
• **Neurologist:** Focuses on the anatomy, functions, and disorders of the nervous system.
</ul

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **present continuous tense**, as indicated by the use of the verb **"is organizing."**
 
• When converting a sentence from active voice to passive voice, the **tense** of the verb must remain the same. For present continuous, the structure becomes **"is/are being + past participle."**
 
• In this case, the subject "The famous art curator" becomes the agent, and the object "A special exhibition" becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.

Correct sentence: *A special exhibition is being organized by the famous art curator, who is known for his unique taste*.

• **Passive Voice Transformation Rules:**

 
 
• **Identify the verb tense:** Ensure the tense remains the same while transforming into passive voice.
 
• **Rearrange the sentence:** The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• **Use appropriate auxiliary verbs:** Add "is/are being" for present continuous tense.
 
• **Add the past participle of the main verb:** Use the third form of the verb.
 
 
 
• **Example of Passive Voice Transformation:**
 
 
• **Active Voice:** The chef is preparing a delicious meal.
 
• **Passive Voice:** A delicious meal is being prepared by the chef.

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?
 The officer was ______ in his conduct, revealing nothing about the investigation into his superior's involvement in several _______ incidents of bribery.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. discreet, discrete .
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The first blank requires a word that describes the officer as being careful and tactful in his behavior. The word **‘discreet’** fits this context perfectly, as it means showing prudence and self-restraint. 
• The second blank requires a word that describes separate or distinct incidents. The word **‘discrete’** is appropriate here, as it means individually separate and distinct. 
• Both words are homonyms, i.e., they sound similar but have different meanings and spellings, making them suitable for this sentence. 
Correct sentence: *The officer was **discreet** in his conduct, revealing nothing about the investigation into his superior's involvement in several **discrete** incidents of bribery.*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Discreet:** 
• **Meaning:** Careful and circumspect in one's speech or actions, especially to avoid causing offense or gaining attention. 
• **Example:** She was very discreet about her personal life. 
• **Usage:** Used to describe someone who exercises caution or prudence. 
• **Discrete:** 
• **Meaning:** Individually separate and distinct. 
• **Example:** The data can be divided into discrete categories. 
• **Usage:** Used in contexts where separation or distinction between entities is emphasized.
